The statements
``<MATH_0001> is separated'',
``<MATH_0002> is a closed immersion'',
``<MATH_0003> is universally closed'', and
``<MATH_0004> is proper''
refer to the notions defined in
Properties of Stacks,
Section <REF_0001>.
Choose a scheme <MATH_0005> and a surjective smooth morphism <MATH_0006>.
Set <MATH_0007> which is an algebraic
space by assumption, and the morphism <MATH_0008> is surjective
and smooth. By
Categories, Lemma <REF_0002>
and
Properties of Stacks,
Lemma <REF_0003>
we see that for any property <MATH_0009> (as in that lemma) we have:
<MATH_0010> has <MATH_0011> if and only if <MATH_0012> has <MATH_0013>.
Hence the equivalence of (2), (3) and (4) follows from
Morphisms of Spaces,
Lemma <REF_0004>
applied to <MATH_0014>.
Moreover, if (1) holds, then <MATH_0015> is separated and we see that
<MATH_0016> is a closed immersion, i.e., (2) holds.
Finally, assume (2) holds. Let <MATH_0017> be a scheme, and <MATH_0018>
a morphism. Set <MATH_0019>. To prove
(1) we have to show that the morphism of algebraic spaces <MATH_0020>
is separated. Using
Categories, Lemma <REF_0005>
once more we see that <MATH_0021> is the base change of
<MATH_0022>. Hence our assumption (2) implies that <MATH_0023>
is a closed immersion, hence <MATH_0024> is separated as desired.
